# Information Security Policy

**Owner:** Sam Whitfield · **Approved:** Maya Chen, 2026-06-26 · **Applies to:** all employees and contractors · **Review:** annually

## Purpose

Stencil holds people's money and identity data. This policy sets the minimum rules for protecting them. Detailed procedures live in the linked docs; this page says what must be true.

## Data classification

| Class | Examples | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| Restricted | SSNs, KYC documents, bank account numbers, card tokens, credentials, DriveWealth positions tied to identity | Encrypted at rest and in transit; access by role only; never in logs, tickets, Slack or Snowflake |
| Confidential | Transaction history, balances, support conversations, internal financials | Access on need-to-know; not shared outside Stencil without NDA |
| Internal | Code, design docs, this wiki | Employees and contractors only |
| Public | Marketing site, published policies | Anyone |

When unsure, treat it as the higher class.

## Access control

- Single sign-on with MFA for every system that supports it. Hardware security keys required for AWS production, GitHub, Pillar Bank portal and DriveWealth back office.
- Least privilege: access is granted for a role and a reason, and removed when either ends.
- Production access is just-in-time where possible; standing production database access is limited to the on-call set.
- Quarterly access reviews per Access Review Procedure.
- Offboarding removes all access within 1 business day; same day for involuntary departures.

## Devices

- Company laptops only for production access, enrolled in MDM with disk encryption, screen lock and timely OS updates (MDM Rollout Plan).
- Lost or stolen device: report in #security within 1 hour.
- No customer Restricted data on laptops, ever.

## Change management

- All production changes go through version control and CI.
- Review requirements per Code Review Standards: two reviewers, one a TL, for money movement and customer financial data.
- Architecture changes need an ADR.
- Production config changes are code changes.

## Logging and monitoring

- Production systems log authentication, authorization failures and admin actions. Logs retained per Data Retention Policy.
- Restricted data is never written to logs. Log scrubbing is tested in CI.
- Alerts route through PagerDuty per On-Call Rotation Design.

## Vendors

- Every vendor that touches Confidential or Restricted data is assessed before contract and reviewed annually (Vendor Risk Register).
- Contracts must include breach notification, data deletion on termination and audit rights.

## Incidents

Report anything suspicious in #security. Response per Incident Response Policy.

## Secure development

- Dependency scanning and static analysis in CI; high and critical findings block merge.
- Secrets live in AWS Secrets Manager or 1Password, never in code or env files committed to repos.
- Annual external penetration test plus targeted tests for major launches.

## Training

Security awareness training at hire and annually; phishing simulations quarterly. Engineers also complete secure coding training covering our stack.

## Exceptions

Exceptions need a written request, a compensating control, an expiry date and Sam's plus Maya's approval. Logged in the exceptions register and reviewed quarterly.

## Enforcement

Violations are handled case by case. Honest mistakes reported promptly are treated as learning; concealment is not.

## Changelog

- 2026-08-31: hardware keys extended to DriveWealth back office ahead of the investing beta; Lithic added to vendor scope.
- 2026-06-26: approved.

Decision: Snowflake is not approved for Restricted data. Any pipeline that would copy Restricted data into Snowflake needs Sam's review first.

- [ ] Sam: publish the exceptions register in this space by 2026-10-16
